messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the design sync — I sketched a ‘resistant SLO backpressure’ variant for Dedicated pools. TL;DR: prefer sustained soft-throttling + burst credits over aggressive eviction for tiered tenants. Thoughts?

devin: can you paste the sketch? not sure I got the exact tradeoff you mean.

maya: sure — main points: 1) maintain a small guaranteed headroom per tenant (configurable), 2) when global pressure spikes use a short soft-throttle (e.g., 2–10s token queueing) before evicting warmups, 3) consume tenant burst credits for >SLO bursts, 4) only evict if queueing + credits both exhausted. so eviction is last resort.

ryan: hmm. so eviction is deprioritized vs throttling. how do we avoid long tail waits for low-latency tenants?

maya: keep per-tenant latency SLO weights; high-weight tenants have stricter headroom and smaller throttle windows. low-weight tenants get longer throttle but more burst credit consumption.

sophia: curious about billing/credits accounting — burst credits are charged differently? we need a clear audit trail for billing + debugging.

maya: yes — credits are consumed from the tenant ledger. tentative rule: credits burn proportional to requests served during throttle window at a multiplier. example: burn = tokens_served * 1.5 during throttling. We log burn events to billing stream with reason tags (throttle|evict|fallback).

devin: do we have signal sources for 'global pressure'? is this operator-driven or autoscaler-driven?

ryan: proposal — a composite pressure signal: (1) cluster free GPU fraction, (2) queue depth growth rate, (3) recent cold-start failures. weighted and smoothed over 10–30s. autoscaler exposes the scalar to orch.

maya: exactly. orch policy subscribes to that scalar. when scalar > threshold enters 'degraded mode' and switches admission to throttle-first.

sophia: edge-case: what about tenants pinned to dedicated capacity (reserved)? should they be exempt?

maya: reserved tenants keep their guaranteed capacity — headroom and throttling only affect non-reserved shares. but reserved can still opt-in to burst consumption if they permit.

devin: rollout concerns: this is a pretty large behavioral change. we should simulate with the autoscaler sim harness and run a canary in a small pool for 48–72h. add feature flag gating.

ops-bot: FYI deploying throttle-first policy without circuit breakers triggered a 15% error spike in canary yesterday at 04:12 UTC (investigating).

ryan: good catch. we need safety nets — fallthrough fallback to preemptible nodes or model-variant routing if latency degrades beyond X%.

sophia: also add tracing tags per request: adm_policy=throttle|evict, burst_credit_used=true/false, headroom_snapshot=<n>. helps debugging.

maya: agree. action items: 1) dev: add simulation scenarios (burst, sustained spike, coldstart cascade) — @devin 2) infra: expose composite pressure scalar to orch — @ryan 3) billing: define credit burn formula + logging schema — @sophia 4) ops: add circuit-breaker fallback + canary runbook — @ops-bot

devin: taking simulation tasks, will push initial harness by EOD tomorrow.

ryan: I'll prototype the pressure exporter and a safe default threshold.

sophia: will draft billing event spec and a couple example logs.

maya: thanks team. next sync Friday to review sim output and canary plan. if ops-bot finds more noisy signals, we pause. :thumbsup:
